prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (ideology-neutral; no parties or individuals named)

Fiscal and tax policy
- Cut the deficit every year, get debt falling, and achieve a current budget surplus as soon as possible; no new borrowing to fund pledges; independent OBR auditing of manifesto costings.
- Reintroduce a 10p income tax starting rate; no increases to basic or higher Income Tax, National Insurance, or VAT; end the Marriage Tax Allowance.
- Raise the top income tax rate for earnings over £150,000; abolish non‑dom status; strengthen anti‑avoidance rules and transparency (including beneficial ownership registers).
- Proceeds from remaining bank share sales to reduce national debt.

Economy, industry and small business
- Maintain a competitive corporation tax rate; cut and then freeze business rates for 1.5m small properties.
- Create a British Investment Bank and regional banks; increase banking competition.
- Establish a National Infrastructure Commission; support HS2 (with cost control), Northern rail links, strategic roads, cycling; rapid decision on SE airport capacity.
- Expand high-speed broadband and mobile coverage nationwide.
- Green strategy: decarbonise electricity by 2030; empower the Green Investment Bank; create an Energy Security Board; robust regime for shale; long-term plan for offshore oil and gas.

Work, pay and skills
- Raise the National Minimum Wage to over £8/hour by Oct 2019; use procurement to promote the Living Wage; reporting on Living Wage by listed firms.
- Ban exploitative zero-hours contracts; close agency worker undercutting loophole; scrap employment tribunal fees system.
- Guarantee an apprenticeship for every school leaver with required grades; require major contractors and large non‑EU skilled sponsors to offer apprenticeships.
- Reduce university tuition fees to £6,000; new Technical Degrees; tackle unpaid internships.
- Compulsory Jobs Guarantee for long‑term unemployed, funded by a bank bonus tax.

Cost of living, markets and housing
- Freeze energy bills until 2017 while reforming the market (ring-fence generation/supply, tougher watchdog); expand home energy efficiency.
- Strengthen water regulation and affordability schemes.
- Rail: allow a public operator to bid; review franchising; fare freeze next year; strict caps; right to the cheapest ticket. Devolve bus powers and smart ticketing.
- Build at least 200,000 homes per year by 2020; first dibs for local first-time buyers; “use it or lose it” powers on land; support small builders; new garden cities.
- Private renting: three‑year tenancies as standard, ceiling on excessive rent rises, ban unfair letting fees, national landlord register.
- Abolish the Bedroom Tax.

Health and social care
- Fund 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 more nurses, 3,000 more midwives via a mansion tax on £2m+ properties, a tobacco levy, and anti‑avoidance.
- 48‑hour GP appointment guarantee; one‑week cancer tests by 2020; Cancer Treatments Fund.
- Integrate physical, mental and social care; parity for mental health; 28‑day access goal for talking therapies; expand school‑based counselling.
- Prevention: action on obesity, alcohol; limits on sugar/salt/fat in foods marketed to children.
- Social care: end 15‑minute visits; recruit 5,000 home‑care workers; identify and support unpaid carers; improve workforce terms.

Education
- Protect the whole education budget (early years to post‑16); cap infant class sizes at 30; all teachers to be qualified; new School Leadership Institute; local Directors of School Standards.
- Strengthen vocational route with a Technical Baccalaureate; English and Maths to 18; improved careers guidance.

Immigration and integration
- Full exit checks; +1,000 border staff (funded by a small charge on non‑visa visitors); retain non‑EU work cap; tighten short‑term student routes; two‑year wait for EU migrants’ benefits; English proficiency for public‑facing staff.
- Ban agencies hiring only from overseas; extend Gangmasters Licensing Authority where abuse exists.

Crime, policing and justice
- Safeguard 10,000 frontline police roles through structural changes; Local Policing Commitment; replace IPCC with a Police Standards Authority; professionalise police/prison officers.
- Victims’ Law; tougher penalties for assaults on public‑facing workers; expand restorative justice; target legal highs; stronger child protection powers.
- Violence against women and girls bill; commissioner; stable refuge and Rape Crisis funding; tighter gun licensing; improved legal aid access.

Constitution, devolution, rights and media
- Constitutional Convention; replace House of Lords with an elected Senate of the Nations and Regions; devolution of £30bn and powers to English regions; extend local planning powers over high streets.
- Implement further powers for Scotland and Wales; fair funding floor for Wales; support NI institutions.
- Votes at 16–17; repeal Lobbying Act and introduce a tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships/consultancies; large firms to publish gender pay gaps.
- Protect the Human Rights Act and ECHR; extend FOI to major outsourced providers; safeguard judicial review.
- Strengthen media plurality rules; implement Leveson; keep Channel 4 in public ownership; maintain free museum entry.

Foreign, defence, development and climate
- Strategic Defence and Security Review in year one; maintain NATO commitment; retain a continuous at‑sea nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Veterans’ Register; outlaw discrimination against service members; embed Military Covenant in NHS.
- EU: focus on reform, single market completion, budget discipline; no Euro; red‑card for national parliaments; referendum lock on any future power transfers.
- Counter‑terrorism with updated powers and oversight; stronger deradicalisation for returnees; overhaul Prevent.
- Human rights envoys for religious freedom and LGBT rights; support two‑state solution; support Afghanistan.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; focus on poorest countries, tax capacity, anti‑corruption; Centre for Universal Health Coverage; lead on UN humanitarian reform.
- Climate diplomacy: push for ambitious Paris deal, five‑yearly strengthening, and global net‑zero emissions in the second half of the century.
